examples.en: You can overlook the downtown area from the observatory.
I climbed to the top and looked out over the village below.
This is a room that overlooks the Han River.

examples.ko: 케이블카를 타면 섬 전체를 조망하며 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: On the cable car, you can take in the whole island as you go.

examples.ko: 높은 곳에서 조망하니까 길이 한눈에 보였어요.
examples.en: Looking out from a high place, I could see the whole road at a glance.

examples.ko: 지난 십 년을 조망해 보는 시간이 필요해요.
examples.en: We need time to take a broad look back at the last ten years.

explain: 높은 곳에서 멀리 넓게 바라본다는 뜻이에요. 일상에서는 '내려다보다', '한눈에 보다'라고 더 많이 말해요. 글에서는 어떤 일의 전체 흐름을 넓게 살펴본다는 비유로도 써서 '역사를 조망하다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I looked down at the city from the rooftop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조망하다와 비슷하게 높은 곳에서 보는 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday word similar to 조망하다 for looking from a high place.

phrases.example: 전망대에서는 시내를 한눈에 볼 수 있어요.
phrases.en: From the observatory you can see the whole downtown at a glance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넓은 곳을 한꺼번에 볼 수 있다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling of seeing a wide area all at once.

phrases.en: This book surveys Korean history as a whole.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일의 전체 흐름을 넓게 살펴본다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for looking broadly at the whole flow of something.

explain_en: Look at a wide view from a high place (도시를 조망하다) It means looking out widely and far from a high place. In daily speech people say '내려다보다' or '한눈에 보다' more often. In writing it is also used figuratively for taking a broad look at the whole flow of something, as in '역사를 조망하다'.

t90.ax: This is a room that overlooks the Han River.

examples.en: The stream trickles along.
The puppy follows its owner around closely.
Water is trickling out of the faucet.

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마 손을 잡고 졸졸 걸어갔어요.
examples.en: The child toddled along after her mother, holding her hand.

examples.ko: 작은 샘에서 맑은 물이 졸졸 솟아요.
examples.en: Clear water bubbles gently from the small spring.

examples.ko: 어린 동생이 하루 종일 졸졸 따라와요.
examples.en: My little sibling tags along behind me all day.

explain: 물이 가늘게 흐르는 소리와, 작은 아이나 동물이 계속 따라다니는 모습 두 가지에 써요. 물이 세게 흐르면 '콸콸', 많이 쏟아지면 '주룩주룩'을 써서 물의 양에 따라 말이 달라요.

phrases.en: Clear water trickles down from the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 가늘게 흐를 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for thinly flowing water.

phrases.en: The child follows Mom around everywhere.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 아이나 동물이 계속 뒤를 따라다니는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a small child or animal that keeps tagging along behind someone.

phrases.example: 물탱크가 거의 비어서 샤워기에서 물이 졸졸 나와요.
phrases.en: The water tank is almost empty, so water only trickles out of the shower.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수도에서 물이 약하게 나올 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used when tap water comes out weakly.

explain_en: It is used both for the sound of thin water flowing and for a small child or animal following closely. Stronger flow is '콸콸' and heavy pouring is '주룩주룩', so the word changes with the amount of water.

examples.en: When spring comes, the trees and plants turn green.
The drought was long, so the vegetation dried up.

examples.ko: 비가 그치자 초목에 맺힌 이슬이 반짝였어요.
examples.en: After the rain stopped, the dew on the plants sparkled.

examples.ko: 이 섬에는 초목도 거의 자라지 않아요.
examples.en: Hardly any vegetation grows on this island.
I walked along a forest path full of the scent of greenery.

examples.ko: 겨울이 되면 초목은 모두 잠을 자는 것 같아요.
examples.en: In winter, it seems all the plants go to sleep.

explain: 나무와 풀을 한꺼번에 말할 때 쓰고, '식물'보다 글 느낌이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '나무랑 풀'이라고 하고, '초목'은 설명하는 글이나 자연 이야기에서 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: When it rains, the plants grow quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무와 풀이 함께 자라는 자연 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes trees and grass growing together in nature.

phrases.en: In winter, the plants wither.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절이나 가뭄 때문에 식물이 힘을 잃는 모습을 글로 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in writing for plants losing vitality due to seasons or drought.

phrases.en: The mountain is full of trees and grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 일상 대화에서 훨씬 쉽고 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but a much easier, more natural phrase for everyday talk.

explain_en: It covers trees and grass together and sounds more literary than '식물' (plants). In everyday talk people say '나무랑 풀', while '초목' appears in descriptive writing and nature topics.

examples.en: In autumn, farmers harvest the rice.

examples.ko: 우리 할아버지는 올해도 직접 쌀을 추수하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandfather harvested the rice himself again this year.

examples.ko: 비가 오기 전에 서둘러 추수해야 해요.
examples.en: We have to hurry and harvest before the rain comes.
After the harvest, the village holds a feast.

examples.ko: 추수할 때가 되자 들판이 노랗게 변했어요.
examples.en: When it was time to harvest, the fields turned yellow.

examples.ko: 다 추수한 논이 텅 비어 보여요.
examples.en: The fully harvested paddy looks empty.

explain: '추수하다'는 가을에 벼 같은 곡식을 거둘 때 써요. '수확하다'는 곡식뿐 아니라 과일과 채소에도 두루 써요. 명사 '추수'로 '추수가 끝나다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: The harvest ended, so the village held a feast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '추수'로 가을 일이 마무리됐다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun '추수' says the autumn harvest work is done.

phrases.example: 추수 때는 온 가족이 일을 도와요.
phrases.en: At harvest time the whole family helps out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곡식을 거두는 바쁜 시기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the busy season of gathering grain.

phrases.en: I cooked rice using this year's harvest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '추수한 + 곡식'으로 막 거둔 곡식을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '추수한 + grain' means grain that was just harvested.

explain_en: Sino-Korean, specific to crops, esp. rice in autumn. '추수하다' is for gathering grain such as rice in autumn. '수확하다' works more broadly, also covering fruit and vegetables. You can also use the noun and say '추수가 끝나다' (the harvest is over).

t90.ax: In autumn, farmers harvest the rice.

examples.en: A sea breeze is blowing, so the beach is cool.
I bought garlic grown in the sea breeze.
The sea breeze blows from the sea to the land during the day.
My hair feels sticky because of the sea breeze.

examples.ko: 이 마을은 해풍에 강한 나무를 심어요.
examples.en: This village plants trees that stand up to the sea wind.
Fish dried in the sea breeze tastes good.

explain: 바다에서 불어오는 바람이에요. 반대로 육지에서 바다 쪽으로 부는 바람은 '육풍'이라고 해요. 농수산물을 소개할 때 '해풍 맞은 ~'라는 표현을 자주 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I took a walk by the sea, feeling the sea breeze.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람을 몸으로 느낀다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most commonly used to mean feeling the breeze on your body.

phrases.en: In the evening, a cool sea breeze blew.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이 부는 상황을 그대로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to simply describe the breeze blowing.

phrases.en: Vegetables grown in the sea breeze have a rich flavor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 농수산물을 소개할 때 자주 보는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen when introducing food and farm or sea products.

explain_en: This is wind blowing in from the sea. The opposite, wind blowing from land to sea, is '육풍'. In product descriptions of farm and sea foods you often see phrases like '해풍 맞은 ~' (sea-breeze-grown).

t90.ax: I bought garlic grown in the sea breeze.

examples.en: They say the bitter cold will continue this week.
Even in the bitter cold, the children played outside.
I bought a thick coat to prepare for the severe cold.
The severe cold did a lot of damage to the crops.

examples.ko: 시베리아의 혹한은 상상도 못 할 정도래요.
examples.en: They say the Siberian cold is beyond imagination.
To get through the severe cold, I didn't hold back on heating costs.

explain: '추위'보다 훨씬 심한, 몸이 견디기 힘든 영하의 추위예요. '한파'는 갑자기 찬 공기가 밀려오는 현상이고, '혹한'은 그 추위가 아주 매섭다는 점을 말해요. 반대말은 '혹서'(몹시 심한 더위)예요.

phrases.en: A severe cold suddenly hit, and the water pipes froze.
phrases.nuance_ko: '닥치다'와 함께 심한 추위가 갑자기 올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '닥치다' when severe cold suddenly arrives.

phrases.en: I bought a thick blanket to prepare for the bitter cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 추위가 오기 전에 준비한다고 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when preparing before the cold arrives.

phrases.example: 이번 주에는 한파가 와서 많이 추워요.
phrases.en: A cold wave is coming this week, so it is very cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: '혹한'보다 일상 뉴스에서 더 자주 쓰고, 갑자기 오는 찬 공기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Seen more often in everyday news; it refers to a sudden mass of cold air.

explain_en: It means cold far harsher than '추위', the kind of freezing weather that is hard to bear. '한파' is a cold wave that suddenly arrives, while '혹한' stresses how severe the cold is. The opposite is '혹서' (extreme heat).

examples.en: Flowers bloomed in the flower bed in front of the apartment.
I take good care of the flower bed.

examples.ko: 화단이 넓어서 꽃을 많이 심을 수 있어요.
examples.en: The flower bed is wide, so I can plant many flowers.
Students look after the school flower bed.
The child picked a flower from the flower bed.
I rested sitting on the bench next to the flower bed.

explain: 땅을 따로 만들어 꽃이나 작은 나무를 심은 곳이 '화단'이고, 그릇에 심은 건 '화분'이에요. 학교나 아파트 앞에서 자주 보이고, '화단을 가꾸다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I plant flowers in the flower bed in spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃을 땅에 직접 심을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when planting flowers directly in the ground.
phrases.en_equiv: to plant flowers in the bed

phrases.en: I water the flower bed every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '물을 주다'는 식물에 물을 준다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Mureul juda' means to water plants.

phrases.en: My grandmother tends the flower bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃을 돌보며 예쁘게 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means caring for flowers and keeping the bed nice.

explain_en: Raised or fenced patch of soil for planting flowers. A patch of ground set aside for flowers or small trees is a 화단, while plants in a container are 화분. You see them at schools and in front of apartments, and say '화단을 가꾸다' (tend a flower bed).

en: to be wound; to be entwined

examples.ko: 담쟁이덩굴이 오래된 집 기둥에 휘감겨 있어요.
examples.en: Ivy is wound around the pillars of the old house.

examples.ko: 긴 목도리가 목에 휘감겨서 조금 답답해요.
examples.en: The long scarf is wrapped around my neck, so it feels a bit stifling.

examples.ko: 산 전체가 짙은 안개에 휘감겨 보이지 않아요.
examples.en: The whole mountain is wrapped in thick fog and can't be seen.
A rope got wound around my foot and I almost fell.

examples.ko: 알 수 없는 불안감에 휘감겨 한숨도 못 잤어요.
examples.en: Gripped by an unexplained anxiety, I couldn't sleep a wink.
While I was swimming, water weeds got tangled around my legs.

explain: 감는 일을 하는 '휘감다'의 피동형이라서 '~에 휘감기다'처럼 조사 '에'와 같이 써요. 줄이나 천 같은 물건뿐 아니라 안개, 불안, 분위기처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것이 몸이나 장소를 감싸는 느낌에도 써요.

phrases.example: 긴 치마가 걸을 때마다 다리에 휘감겨요.
phrases.en: The long skirt wraps around my legs every time I walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~에 휘감기다'로 쓰고 감기는 대상이 앞에 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as '~에 휘감기다', with the thing being wrapped before it.

phrases.en: Vines are wrapped all around the tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감긴 상태가 계속될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the wrapped state continues.

phrases.en: It was cold, so I wrapped a scarf around my neck.
phrases.nuance_ko: '휘감기다'의 능동형이에요. 내가 직접 감을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form of 휘감기다, used when you do the wrapping yourself.

explain_en: It is the passive of '휘감다' (to wind around), so it is used with the particle '에', as in '~에 휘감기다'. Besides things like rope or cloth, it also describes unseen things such as fog, anxiety or an atmosphere enveloping a person or place.

examples.en: The farmer scatters seeds over the field.
Rain sprinkled lightly from the morning and stopped soon after.
The children scattered flower petals on the road.

examples.ko: 케이크 위에 가루 설탕을 살짝 흩뿌려 주세요.
examples.en: Please sprinkle a little powdered sugar on the cake.
I made a painting by flinging paint across the canvas.

examples.ko: 봄바람이 꽃가루를 흩뿌리는 바람에 재채기가 계속 나요.
examples.en: The spring wind is spreading pollen around, so I keep sneezing.

explain: 씨앗, 꽃잎, 가루, 물방울처럼 작은 것을 여기저기 넓게 뿌린다는 느낌이에요. 비나 눈이 가볍게 날릴 때 '비가 흩뿌리다'처럼 목적어 없이도 써요. 그냥 '뿌리다'보다 흩어지는 모습이 더 잘 그려져요.

phrases.en: The wind scattered petals over the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃잎처럼 작고 가벼운 것을 넓게 뿌리는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes spreading small, light things like petals widely.

phrases.en: Snow has been flurrying since this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈이나 비가 가볍게 날릴 때 목적어 없이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used without an object when snow or rain falls lightly.

phrases.en: The dog shook itself and sprayed water droplets everywhere.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 물방울이 사방으로 튀는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes small droplets spraying in all directions.

explain_en: It gives the image of small things such as seeds, petals, powder or drops being spread widely here and there. It can also be used without an object, as in '비가 흩뿌리다' (rain drizzles in light sprays). Compared with plain '뿌리다', the scattering picture is clearer.

t90.ax: The farmer scatters seeds over the field.

examples.en: Modern Korean history has passed through an era of upheaval.
My grandmother grew up going through war and upheaval.
I read the story of a generation born in a turbulent period.

examples.ko: 세상이 빠르게 변하는 격동 속에서 길을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm trying to find my way amid the turbulence of a fast-changing world.
Investors are anxious because of the turmoil in the market.

examples.ko: 격동의 시기가 지나고 나라가 다시 안정을 찾았어요.
examples.en: After the period of upheaval passed, the country regained stability.

explain: 사회나 시대가 크게 흔들리며 빠르게 변할 때 써요. '격동의 시대', '격동기'처럼 굳어진 말이 많고, 개인의 가벼운 변화에는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.en: My grandfather lived through a turbulent period.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사회가 크게 흔들리고 빠르게 변하던 시기를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a period when society was shaken and changing quickly.

phrases.en: A lot happened in that turbulent era.
phrases.nuance_ko: '격동' 뒤에 '의'를 붙여 시대를 꾸미는 굳어진 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase using 의 after 격동 to describe an era.

phrases.en: My grandmother lived through the upheaval of war.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 흔들리는 시대를 직접 지나왔다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone personally went through a time of great upheaval.

explain_en: It is used when a society or era is shaken and changes rapidly. Fixed phrases such as '격동의 시대' and '격동기' are common, and it is rarely used for small personal changes.

en: to rally; to unite; to gather together

examples.en: Citizens gathered in the square and cheered as one.
When fans band together, it becomes a great force.

examples.ko: 위기 때 사람들의 힘을 결집하는 것이 중요해요.
examples.en: In a crisis, it is important to bring people's strength together.
The candidate toured the country to rally his supporters.

examples.ko: 학생들이 한곳에 결집하고 있다는 소식이 들렸어요.
examples.en: I heard news that students are gathering in one place.
Thanks to the residents banding together, the plan was cancelled.

explain: '모이다'와 달리 흩어져 있던 사람이나 힘이 한 가지 목적으로 뭉치는 느낌이에요. '힘을 결집하다', '지지층을 결집하다'처럼 자주 쓰고, 뉴스나 선거 이야기에 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 우리는 힘을 결집해서 이 문제를 해결했어요.
phrases.en: We pooled our strength and solved this problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람의 힘을 한 가지 목적으로 모은다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to gather many people's strength toward a single goal.

phrases.example: 모두 한마음으로 뭉쳐서 어려움을 이겨 냈어요.
phrases.en: Everyone came together as one and overcame the difficulty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결집하다'와 뜻이 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning to 결집하다 but more casual in daily speech.

phrases.en: This team has strong cohesion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 하나로 뭉치는 힘을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the power that holds people together as one.

explain_en: Abstract rallying of people or forces into one body (광장에 결집하다) Unlike plain '모이다' (to gather), it carries the feel of scattered people or forces uniting for one purpose. It is common in phrases like '힘을 결집하다' (pool strength) and '지지층을 결집하다' (rally supporters), and shows up a lot in the news and election talk.

t90.ax: When fans band together, it becomes a great force.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 고위급 회담이 내일 열려요.
examples.en: The high-level talks between the two countries will be held tomorrow.
High-ranking officials have just arrived at the event hall.
I heard the high-ups decided this matter themselves.
A high-ranking official visited the site yesterday.
It's a meeting attended by top officials, so security is strict.
The high-level delegation is scheduled to return in the afternoon.

explain: 뉴스에서 '고위급 회담', '고위급 인사'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여 가장 많이 들려요. 회사 이야기보다는 정부나 국가 사이의 일에 더 자주 쓰여요. 반대로 실무자 수준은 '실무급'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: A high-ranking official attended the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 자리에 있는 사람을 가리킬 때 가장 흔히 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to refer to people in high positions.

phrases.example: 고위급 회담이 끝난 뒤 두 정부가 발표를 했어요.
phrases.en: After the high-level talks ended, the two governments made an announcement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국가나 정부 사이의 회의를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for meetings between countries or governments.

phrases.en: A high-ranking civil servant visited the accident site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정부에서 높은 직급인 공무원을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to civil servants of high rank in the government.

explain_en: Noun used before nouns for level of talks/officials (고위급 회담); about rank level, not people. You hear it most in the news before a noun, as in '고위급 회담' and '고위급 인사'. It is used more for government and international matters than for company talk. The opposite level, working-level staff, is called '실무급'.

t90.ax: A high-ranking official visited the site yesterday.

examples.ko: 두 나라 사이에 군사적 긴장이 높아졌어요.
examples.en: Military tension rose between the two countries.

examples.ko: 그 섬은 군사적으로 매우 중요한 곳이에요.
examples.en: That island is a very important place militarily.

examples.ko: 군사적인 방법만으로는 문제를 풀 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't solve the problem with military means alone.
We have to solve it in a non-military way.
The internet originally started for military purposes.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 군사적 가치가 높아서 관리가 엄격해요.
examples.en: This area has high military value, so it is strictly managed.

explain: '군사'와 관련된 일이나 성격을 말할 때 쓰고, 뉴스와 설명하는 글에서 많이 나와요. '군사적 긴장', '군사적 목적'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸미거나 '군사적으로'로 써요. 반대로 쓰는 말은 '평화적'이에요.

phrases.example: 이 기술은 군사적 목적으로 처음 만들어졌어요.
phrases.en: This technology was first made for military purposes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '군사적' 뒤에 명사가 와서 어떤 일의 목적을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies a noun to describe the purpose of something.

phrases.example: 두 나라는 군사적 충돌을 피하려고 대화했어요.
phrases.en: The two countries talked to avoid a military clash.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 나라 사이의 싸움을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in news when talking about fighting between countries.

phrases.en: That country is very strong militarily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '군사적으로'는 '군사 면에서'라는 뜻으로 서술어를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: '군사적으로' means 'in military terms' and modifies the predicate.

explain_en: Adjective-like form meaning military in nature, placed before a noun (군사적 훈련); formal, used in news and writing. It describes things connected to the military and is common in news and explanatory writing. It modifies a noun, as in '군사적 긴장' and '군사적 목적', or becomes '군사적으로'. A natural opposite is '평화적' (peaceful).

t90.ax: We have to solve it in a non-military way.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 물밑에서 계속 협상하고 있어요.
examples.en: The two countries keep negotiating behind the scenes.

examples.ko: 물밑 접촉 끝에 드디어 합의가 나왔어요.
examples.en: After behind-the-scenes contacts, an agreement was finally reached.
The news spread quickly under the surface.

examples.ko: 물밑 작업 덕분에 일이 순조롭게 풀렸어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the groundwork behind the scenes, things went smoothly.
The diver carefully examined the area under the water.
A reporter was the first to notice the activity beneath the surface.

explain: 뉴스에서는 대부분 '물밑 협상', '물밑 접촉', '물밑 작업'처럼 겉으로 드러나지 않게 진행하는 일을 말해요. 반대 느낌은 '수면 위로 드러나다', '공개적으로'예요. 물속 아래라는 원래 뜻도 있지만 일상 대화에서는 비유로 더 많이 들어요.

phrases.example: 두 회사가 물밑 협상을 이어가고 있어요.
phrases.en: The two companies are continuing behind-the-scenes talks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 드러나지 않게 하는 협상이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negotiations held out of public view.

phrases.example: 이번 계약은 오랜 물밑 작업 끝에 나왔어요.
phrases.en: This contract came after a long period of quiet groundwork.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드러나지 않게 준비하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to preparation done quietly out of sight.

phrases.en: People worked hard behind the scenes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용히 일을 진행할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when things are being carried out quietly.

explain_en: In the news it is mostly used in phrases like '물밑 협상' (behind-the-scenes talks), '물밑 접촉' and '물밑 작업' for things done out of public view. The opposite feel is '수면 위로 드러나다' (come to the surface) or doing something publicly. It also literally means under the water, but you hear the figurative use more in daily talk.
